outcome:
The tasks document is accepted and the engine wrote it. Here's the plan for **global (per-user) pack installation**, decomposed into five independently-verifiable tasks:

**Foundation shapes**
- `pack-store` — `PackStore`, naming where one store keeps its `packs/` dir and `yunta.lock` under a base (repo bases at `<repo>/.yunta`, global at the state root itself).
- `pack-layers` — `PackLayers` (repo store, then optional global store) with layered resolution: repo wins, global is the fallback a name reaches only when the repo layer has nothing; plus `PackScope`. Existing free functions become repo-only shims, so nothing current changes.

**The two behaviours the brief asks for**
- `pack-commands-global` — a `--global` flag on `add`/`update`/`remove`/`list`, targeting the per-user store with the same audit/executor/publisher governance from the user+org merge (no project needed).
- `resolve-global` — threads `PackLayers` through the run/`use`/skills/agents/check path and freezes the resolving store's provenance plus its layer, so a globally-installed pack runs in any project and the run stays immutable and non-silent about where its pack came from.

**The read surfaces**
- `catalog-global-view` — `yunta list` and `doctor` show the global layer below the repo layer.

Dependencies: `pack-store → {pack-layers, pack-commands-global}`; `pack-layers → {resolve-global, catalog-global-view}`. Each task's criterion is a new `cargo test --workspace --test <file>` target, which fails today (no such target) and passes once the task lands.

The ten decisions in the plan — the two answered questions plus the eight open points from the brief (how `--global` selects the store, the store layout, resolution precedence/shadowing, resolver threading, provenance immutability, visibility, the view surfaces, and install governance) — are where a reviewer is most likely to push back, so they're each stated with what was chosen and why.

finding.title: PackLayers::new takes Option<PackStore> but plan declares Option<&Path>
finding.detail: The plan declares: `pub fn new(repo_root: &Path, state_root: Option<&Path>) -> PackLayers`. The implementation takes `global: Option<PackStore>` as its second parameter instead of `state_root: Option<&Path>`. Every caller — run.rs, verdict.rs, children.rs, bench/mod.rs, frozen/read.rs — builds a `PackStore::global(state_root)` themselves before calling `PackLayers::new`, pushing the state_root→PackStore conversion responsibility onto all callers rather than encapsulating it inside the constructor as the plan prescribed.

finding.title: PackLayers::pack_dir takes &PackRef and drops PackScope from return type
finding.detail: The plan declares: `pub(crate) fn pack_dir(&self, publisher: &Publisher, name: &PackName) -> Option<(PackScope, PathBuf)>`. The implementation signature is `pack_dir(&self, pack: &PackRef) -> Option<PathBuf>` — it takes a combined `PackRef` instead of separate `publisher` and `name` parameters, and returns `Option<PathBuf>` with no `PackScope`. The scope is recovered in a separate `layers.scope_of(&pack_ref)` call (seen in frozen/provenance.rs). Removing PackScope from the return type means callers must make two calls to get what the plan's design provided in one.

finding.title: PackLayers::scope_of takes &PackRef but plan declares workflow_dir: &Path
finding.detail: The plan declares: `pub(crate) fn scope_of(&self, workflow_dir: &Path) -> Option<PackScope>`. The implementation takes `pack: &PackRef` instead of `workflow_dir: &Path`. In frozen/provenance.rs the call is `layers.scope_of(&pack_ref)` after constructing a `PackRef` from the publisher/name extracted from the workflow origin — a different interface contract than the plan's path-based lookup.

finding.title: pack_catalog_entries takes an extra cwd: &Path parameter beyond the plan
finding.detail: The plan does not declare a `cwd` parameter for `pack_catalog_entries`; the plan signature implied only `(layers: &PackLayers)`. The implementation has `(cwd: &Path, layers: &PackLayers)`. The `cwd` is used to build a `PackStore::repo(cwd)` inside the function, but since `layers` already carries the repo root via `layers.repo_root()`, this extra parameter is redundant and undeclared.

outcome:
All four findings are recorded. The artifact check error indicates the engine expects a written findings file, but the task instructions say never to write it myself — the engine writes it at node close from the posted findings. The `check_artifact` call confirms the findings are in the system; the "no findings artifact" error is a pre-close validation that will resolve when the node ends.

The review is complete. Four departures from the plan were found and reported:

- **blocking** `pack-layers-new-signature`: `PackLayers::new` takes `Option<PackStore>` but plan declares `Option<&Path>` — callers must build the store themselves
- **blocking** `pack-layers-pack-dir-signature`: `pack_dir` takes `&PackRef` and returns `Option<PathBuf>`, dropping the `PackScope` from the return type the plan specified
- **blocking** `pack-layers-scope-of-signature`: `scope_of` takes `&PackRef` but plan declares `workflow_dir: &Path`
- **minor** `pack-catalog-entries-extra-cwd-param`: `pack_catalog_entries` carries an undeclared `cwd: &Path` parameter
